title: Cross-language playbook: shadow credentials, key erasure, and streaming-resume for SDK auth
creator: Priya Desai
description: Deliver a cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) playbook and SDK changes that combine: 1) a 'shadow-credentials' rotation pattern for enterprises (short-lived shadow keys exchanged via SSO/OIDC), 2) language-specific secrets-in-memory erasure APIs, and 3) streaming resume tokens and graceful reconnect semantics so long-lived streams survive credential rotation. The goal is an auditable, ergonomic, and secure auth surface that covers hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and minimizes developer friction for rotation and local development.
background: We have lots of ad-hoc guidance and multiple tickets about rotation, ephemeral tokens, and stream reauth (see dependencies). Customers using Dedicated and Private want automatic key rotation without dropping active streaming sessions. Existing SDKs refresh credentials but either drop streams or keep long-lived in-memory secrets reachable by GC. This ticket unifies a pattern: issue shadow, short-lived creds that shadow a long-term enterprise key; expose a small language-level API erase_secret(); and define a resume_token handshake for streaming so a stream can be resumed after a credential swap. This is not a spec for server-side rotation; it's the SDK-side ergonomics and explicit developer APIs.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) expose a documented rotateShadowCredentials() flow and examples for enterprise SSO desktop flow
A secrets API (erase_secret / zero_memory / clearBytes) exists with language-idiomatic names and unit tests for each SDK
Streaming APIs accept a resume_token and can reconnect without losing in-flight messages when shadow credentials rotate
E2E demo app (chat + streaming embeddings) on Dedicated shows zero user-visible interruption during scheduled rotation (metrics dashboard + smoke tests)
Design reviewed and approved by Security and PM; security checklist items marked resolved
Public docs + migration guide for customers and internal sample repos updated
Performance regression <3% token throughput for common batching profiles when using new auth handshake
implementation_notes: Design decisions: prefer 'shadow-credentials' naming over 'ephemeral-ssotoken' for clarity in logs and auditing; shadow creds are short-lived API keys minted by our control plane with an aud claim linking to the enterprise principal

Python: provide secrets.erase_secret(bytearray) + contextmanager secret_context(bytes_like) that overwrites buffers; avoid relying on GC semantics. Use memoryview where possible. Add unit tests exercising CPython internals on Linux/macOS (Windows behavior documented).

TypeScript: expose SecretBuffer.clear() that zeroes a Uint8Array; document limits in Node.js vs browsers. For browser SDK we fall back to letting the JS runtime GC with a warning in docs (can't reliably overwrite V8-managed strings).

Go: provide secure.Clear(b []byte) and recommend usage patterns in examples; avoid exposing bytes after calls to client constructors. Add lints in examples to detect accidental captures of secrets into closures.

Streaming resume handshake: token included in initial stream metadata and rotated via a small reauth RPC that returns a resume_token signed by control plane. Client should: attach new shadow creds, call stream.Reauth(resume_token), call stream.ResumeAt(seq) — server validates token and rebinds session. If server cannot resume, fall back to graceful restart with a short buffer replay policy.

Rotation agent: implement 'shadow-rotator' helper in SDKs (opt-in) that can be run as a background coroutine/goroutine in customer apps. Rotator observes token TTL, prefetches new shadow creds, performs in-process swap using atomic pointer, triggers reauth on active streams with minimal interruption. For security-sensitive deployments, rotator can be implemented out-of-process (sidecar) — document trade-offs.

Telemetry: emit structured events: auth.rotate.start, auth.rotate.success, auth.rotate.fail, stream.resume.attempt, stream.resume.success, stream.resume.fail. Keep PII out of telframe; include only non-sensitive ids and durations.

Compatibility: new APIs must work with existing hosted API and with dedicated/private control plane where shadow-mint endpoints vary. Add server capability flag for 'supports_stream_resume' to avoid clients attempting resume against older infra.

Trade-offs: attempted in-memory erasure increases code complexity and may not be possible in all runtimes. We will document residual risks and recommended operational mitigations (short TTLs, sidecar rotation for high-security installs).
updates: 2025-11-06: Kickoff — scoped cross-language requirements and confirmed ownership: Liang (SDK runtime), Marco (backend/minting), Nina (security). Decided on 'shadow' naming and resume_token approach.

2025-11-20: Spike complete — proof-of-concept in Python shows stream can resume using resume_token signed by control plane. Issues found around CPython internals for zeroing memory; added task to widen test matrix.

2025-12-08: UX review with PM/Design — agreed to keep SDK surface minimal: rotateShadowCredentials() + optional rotator helper. Design asked for clearer telemetry events — added structured event names.

2026-01-14: Security review (initial) — security requested explicit threat model and requested deterministic erasure tests for supported platforms. Marked security_review_required and added follow-ups to implementation notes.
2026-02-02: TypeScript implementation approved in PR; Node + Deno supported. Browser fallback documented. Added automated lint to flag storing secrets on global scope in example code.
2026-02-25: Go implementation merged behind an opt-in flag in the client. Added resume_token handshake to gRPC metadata path; backend change rolled to staging.

2026-03-03: End-to-end Dedicated smoke run — rotation executed during a live demo with zero dropped user-visible messages in 7/8 runs. One failure was due to old control plane instance without supports_stream_resume flag; added guard in client.
2026-03-10: PR for unified docs published. Security asked for final runbook for incident response related to leaked shadow creds — assigned to Nina (security).
